pr_title: planner: support sql_select_limit session / global variable
pr_body:
<!-- Thank you for contributing to TiDB!

PR Title Format:
1. pkg [, pkg2, pkg3]: what's changed
2. *: what's changed

-->

### What problem does this PR solve?

Issue Number: close #17087 

Problem Summary:
sql_select_limit restricts the max count of select results for select and union statements

### What is changed and how it works?

Proposal: [sql_select_limit](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1h98-nHQo32Qh7w_pbnV9p4jnsuVZh-nblYkL8y_Dg48/edit?usp=sharing)

What's Changed:

Add a TryAddExtraLimit after `Preprocess` and before `Optimize`

How it Works:

It changes ast for SELECT and UNION directly, which is the fastest way to modify.

### Check List <!--REMOVE the items that are not applicable-->

Tests <!-- At least one of them must be included. -->

- Unit test


Side effects

- Plan Bind : After activing this function, plan bind will not work for correctness and safety.
- Plan Cache for prepare : TiDB will not use or update plan cache for prepare, but rebuild the plan for prepare statement.

### Release note <!-- bugfixes or new feature need a release note -->
-Support sql_select_limit session / global vairable

Hi Feng,
What do you suggest to start working on this?

1. A global and session scope variable should be added in [here](https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/838de2ad26a1e494b7b7ed102004eaa3c5510fef/sessionctx/variable/sysvar.go) and [here](https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/997b986387283d68713f50a3cdf5d44abbfccb5a/session/session.go#L1973)
2. If the original plan is a _SELECT_ statement and has no _LIMIT_ Plan on top of it, handle this variable, and add a _LIMIT_ Plan  on top of the original plan in this [file](https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/746c88a461aef16e043348cf1c8a96522f971928/planner/optimize.go)
3. The _EXECUTE_ statement should be considered carefully because the additional _Limit_ Plan should not be cached. Consider this case, 
```mysql
mysql> set session sql_select_limit = 2;
Query OK, 0 rows affected (0.00 sec)

mysql> prepare p1 from 'select * from t1';
Query OK, 0 rows affected (0.00 sec)
Statement prepared

mysql> EXECUTE p1;
+------+------+
| id   | sex  |
+------+------+
|    1 | F    |
|    2 | F    |
+------+------+
2 rows in set (0.01 sec)

mysql> set session sql_select_limit = 3;
Query OK, 0 rows affected (0.00 sec)

mysql> EXECUTE p1;
+------+------+
| id   | sex  |
+------+------+
|    1 | F    |
|    2 | F    |
|    3 | F    |
+------+------+
3 rows in set (0.00 sec)
```
